newsitem.title: UK: UK policy news may aid stg Eurobond sales in Asia.
newsitem.headline: UK policy news may aid stg Eurobond sales in Asia.

text.p: Asian interest in sterling Eurobonds could be boosted by the currency's positive reaction on Tuesday to a British rate rise and news of greater independence for the country's central bank.
Dealers said Asian investors have been buying sterling bonds for two reasons -- as a European currency diversification play ahead of EMU and for its high yield.
"None of what's happened or been said today has done anything to affect that outlook," a Japanese bank syndicate manager said.
Asian investors, while not big buyers, were among the few to show interest in sterling Eurobonds during Britain's lengthy election campaign, dealers said.
"They missed the boat earlier this year," a British bank Eurobond trader said. "But this should give them the confidence to get in properly now."

British finance minister Gordon Brown raised the base lending rate by 0.25 point to 6.25 percent and said from now on the Bank of England -- rather than himself -- would decide interest rate policy in future.
These, and accompanying measures, saw gilt futures over two points higher by 1300 GMT, while cash gilts moved up in line and allowed sterling/mark to set a 57-month high.
The pound's fresh high above 2.83 marks came after a rally that has taken it from a low at 2.2750 marks last August. Sterling ended 1996 around 2.64 marks.

"We've not being seeing any sterling paper coming back even though some (Asian) clients have big profits they could book," a Japanese bank bond trader said. "They're obviously quite happy to hold the currency."
Although British government bond yields tightened sharply today relative to German Bunds, they still offer investors around 1.5 percent more in yield.

After a buoyant start to the year, the sterling Eurobond market has dragged its heels and most new issues have been pretty much domestic affairs. Former Conservative Prime Minister John Major called an election on March 17.
But among the limited sterling issuance with an international flavouring during the election campaign, were also deals specifically structured for and targeted at Japanese retail investor demand.
These short-dated bonds were launched by top-notch credits such as Oesterreichische Kontrollbank and Swedish Export Credit Corp and lead managed by Japanese firms.
Another such issue, a 100 million stg three-year offering with a 6.40 percent semi-annual coupon, was launched this morning by Electricite de France via Nomura International.
The pound's strength was the driving force behind a buoyant first quarter for the sterling Eurobond market.
European investors rushed to buy short-dated sterling paper as the pound's good run on foreign exchanges showed few signs of abating.
Sterling scooped a 13.4 percent share ($26.4 billion) of the international bond market in the first quarter of the year. Sterling bonds accounted for 7.3 percent of the total market in all 1996.
